clue.text: Infantile, shit robber is $1000 down without a robbery

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the shortened name goes round the robbery
with down, says the robber's name is short by the sum that follows, so that letter goes
being down a sum means having lost it, so the robber's surname loses that letter

parts.note: Ronnie Biggs was one of the Great Train Robbers of 1963
a grand, written G
a job is criminal slang for a robbery

explanation.surface: A sneer at some childish crook who has lost a thousand dollars without even pulling off a heist.
explanation.walkthrough: The robber is not a generic thief but Ronnie Biggs, the famous British train robber; take one G off his name and wrap it round JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Big jobs is the nursery euphemism parents use for a bowel movement, so it is a childish word for faeces.

clue.text: The type who'd easily attract a young woman to the bar

definitions.text: The type who'd easily attract a young woman to the bar

parts.note: babe is slang for an attractive young woman
a magnet is the type of thing that draws others to it; a bar magnet is one type of magnet

explanation.surface: A description of the kind of man who can lure girls into the pub with no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe is slang for an attractive young woman; a magnet in slang is someone who draws others, and a bar is also a type of magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a man, or a thing such as a sports car, that reliably draws attractive young women towards him.

clue.text: Seat — the source of many a politician's speech?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the backside one sits on

definitions.text: the source of many a politician's speech?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: politicians are said to talk out of their backsides, that is, to talk nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: Seat looks like a parliamentary seat, which fits the politician; it is the body part. Arse is the British spelling of ass.
explanation.definitionFit: The crude British word for the buttocks, and the place a person talking rubbish is said to speak from.

clue.text: Plied with pub meals, threw up

parts.note: the bar is the drinking room of a pub
plied with food, here the pub meals, means fed

explanation.surface: Someone stuffed with pub grub and then sick, a familiar end to a British night out.
explanation.walkthrough: Plied with pub meals is bar-fed, fed at the bar; meals only finishes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Barf is American-born slang for vomiting, so the past tense matches threw up.

clue.text: Maurice, suffering with DTs, gets pissed

indicators.note: suffering means in a bad way, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
delirium tremens, the shakes of an alcoholic; the setter has counted it as D, T, T

explanation.surface: Poor Maurice, shaking with delirium tremens, gets drunk again.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters do not quite add up: MAURICE plus DTS has an S where the answer needs a second T, so the setter has slipped. Pissed here means urinated, not drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To micturate is the medical verb for urinating, and piss is the vulgar word for the same act.

clue.text: Piss taken out of ' Pop Sails' ( Rolling Stone ) …

indicators.note: rolling means turning over and over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the four letters spelling the first word are lifted one by one out of the quoted title

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Reads like a Private Eye jibe at a pop magazine story, mocking Rolling Stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Piss-take means mockery, but here the four letters really are taken out; Rolling Stone splits into indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone, prized for its shifting play of colours.

clue.text: … "a pop group-stifled drug-affected exercise"

indicators.note: the group smothers the next word, holding it inside

parts.note: Steps was a British pop group of the late 1990s
up is slang for high on drugs

explanation.surface: Continues the previous headline: a story about a pop band smothering some druggy fitness routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the clue before, but the wordplay stands alone. STEPS were a chart-topping British pop group around 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: A step-up is a gym move in which you step on and off a raised block, a common workout drill.

clue.text: Sticking one finger's end right in, one approaches behind

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: with in, says the letters that follow are pushed inside the word that comes next
completes the instruction to stick the short letters inside another word

parts.note: comes near, as a verb: nears
one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, and only that letter is used here

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude picture of an intimate examination by someone creeping up from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind is not a bottom here but the sense of late with payments. The first one is A and the second is I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in arrears is to be overdue with money owed, which is falling behind with payments.

clue.text: Begging-letter from temptress after bonk fails to reach climax

indicators.note: the temptress is written after the shortened word
the word stops short of its last letter, its climax

parts.note: bonk and screw are both British slang for having sex
Eve tempted Adam with the apple in Genesis

explanation.surface: A pleading note from a seductress after a disappointing night in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A screeve is an old slang word for a begging letter, the sort a con artist writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Screeve is nineteenth-century cant for a written appeal for money, such as a beggar's petition.

clue.text: Russian leader's somewhat misplaced contribution

indicators.note: put out of place, so the five letters are reordered

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, Russian president when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A dig at whatever the Russian president has contributed to world affairs, said to be off target.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone puts into a joint effort, a synonym for a contribution.

clue.text: Gilbert & George openings sounded hell

indicators.note: said out loud, the plural Gs comes out as an exclamation

parts.note: the first letters of the two names are two Gs

explanation.surface: Says the private views of the artists Gilbert and George were a nightmare to sit through.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and George are a London artist duo. Their initials make two Gs, and Gs spoken sounds like the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cries of exasperation; jeez is a minced oath for Jesus, used just as one shouts hell.

clue.text: Cardinal donning female underwear in a position to catch something?

definitions.text: in a position to catch something?

indicators.note: the first word puts on the underwear, which is placed after it

parts.note: cardinal in the sense of chief or foremost
a slip is a woman's undergarment

explanation.surface: A cardinal of the church in lingerie, nicely placed to pick up an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: First slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, there to take catches; the question mark points to catching a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: First slip is the close fielder whose whole job in cricket is to hold catches off the edge of the bat.

clue.text: Sang note followed by identical notes during shag

indicators.note: the notes come in the middle of the word for sex

parts.note: bed is used as a verb for having sex with someone

indicators.note: the note comes first and the pair after it

parts.note: la is the sixth note in do-re-mi
B twice, a musical note repeated

explanation.surface: Someone sang a note and then a pair of matching notes in the middle of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Sang is underworld slang for informing on someone, not singing a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing to the police and to blab both mean giving away secrets, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Throw up on becoming engaged — reprimand follows

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first part sits on top of the second
in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw high
parts lock when they engage, like gears or a key in a lock

explanation.surface: Someone vomits just as they get engaged, and a telling-off follows.
explanation.walkthrough: Throw up looks like vomiting; it is a throw read upwards. Bollocking is British slang for a severe telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A bollocking is a severe dressing-down in British slang, the vulgar form of a rollicking.

clue.text: Fear about pubic region organ protection

indicators.note: the first letter is brought round to the end of the word

parts.note: taken as written
the lap is the part of the lower body between waist and knees when seated

explanation.surface: Fear for the groin leads to a box worn to protect a man's organ.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ suggests the penis after pubic region; it is the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear-flap is a hat's side panel that covers and protects the ear, which is an organ of hearing.

clue.text: Cliff providing opportunity for humiliated Romeo to go down?

definitions.text: Cliff providing opportunity for humiliated Romeo
definitions.meaning: a rejected suitor may throw himself off a cliff
the question mark hints at the sexual sense of going down on someone

explanation.walkthrough: Many high cliffs carry the name, from tales of jilted lovers jumping to their deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers' Leap is the traditional name for a cliff from which spurned lovers are said to have leapt.

clue.text: Obsessively motionless?

definitions.meaning: first reading: fussily fixated on order, tidiness and detail, a Freudian personality type
read literally, holding back what the bowels would pass, so having no bowel motions

explanation.walkthrough: Motion is the medical word for a bowel movement, so motionless reads as constipated.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's term for a personality fixated on control, said to stem from withholding faeces in toilet training.

clue.text: Sex tremendous, having relentless secretion

indicators.note: something secreted is hidden away, so the answer is concealed in the words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Great sex with a constant flow of bodily fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: Secretion looks like a bodily fluid; it is the act of secreting, hiding the answer inside sex tremendous.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme measures and relentless ones both go as far as possible without letting up.

clue.text: Not the definitive rock band's rock band reference book

indicators.note: the definite article is dropped from the band's name

parts.note: The Who's, the band's name with its definite article
The Who, the British rock group

explanation.surface: Sounds like a music critic's verdict on the greatest rock band of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Definitive puns on the definite article, the word the. Who's Who is the British directory of notable people.
explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is an annual biographical directory of prominent people, a standard reference work.

clue.text: Hack on the way out, going against the current

parts.note: a hack is a journalist; ED is the editor of one
dying, near death

explanation.surface: A journalist on his last legs who still swims against the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water running counter to the main stream, so eddying water goes against the current.

clue.text: Rails against cryptic-style shit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: attacks angrily in words
second meaning: as a crossword clue, the phrase would be an anagram of hits, giving the swear word

explanation.walkthrough: In crossword terms out signals an anagram, so the answer itself reads as a clue for the swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit out at something is to criticise it fiercely, which is what railing against means.

clue.text: Shook, going double topless and sporting tits

indicators.note: losing its top letter twice over, so the first two letters go

parts.note: shuddered, trembled

explanation.surface: A woman trembling as she strips off and shows her breasts.
explanation.walkthrough: Tits here are teats, as on a cow; uddered means having an udder.
explanation.definitionFit: Uddered means having an udder, and an udder carries the teats, which crude slang calls tits.

clue.text: Comes back to life and pants?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., the opposite of dies
second meaning: underwear, which pants means in British English

explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British for underpants, not trousers or panting. The question mark flags the made-up verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is the colloquial word for underwear, which British speakers also call pants.

clue.text: Junkie has to swipe loaf

parts.note: a swipe is a blow, a smack
loaf is slang for the head, from rhyming slang loaf of bread

explanation.surface: An addict who is driven to steal a loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Swipe and loaf both pretend to be about theft and bread. Smack is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A smackhead is British slang for a heroin addict, smack being heroin, so a junkie.

clue.text: Brief shot perhaps of American ex-Minister

parts.note: Mo Mowlam, the former Northern Ireland Secretary

explanation.surface: A short snapshot of a former US cabinet member.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Mowlam was a much-loved British Labour minister who had just left office.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is the clipped form of ammunition, and shot is one kind of ammunition, hence brief.

clue.text: Goodness calls for a lot of money, a lot of money

indicators.note: the grand is called in to stand in place of one letter

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
a grand, G

explanation.surface: Exclaims that something demands a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The L replaced is the pound sign's letter, so a grand stands in for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Golly and goodness are both mild exclamations of surprise used in place of God.

clue.text: Bottle internal organs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: courage, in British slang
second meaning: the intestines or innards

explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve, from rhyming slang; it has nothing to do with a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts means both nerve, as in having the guts, and the intestines inside the body.

clue.text: Virgin's temporary barrier means Carol possibly carrying last bit of luggage

indicators.note: the hymn holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a carol is one kind of hymn

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of luggage

explanation.surface: Suggests a barrier at Virgin Atlantic check-in, held up by a woman called Carol with her bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgin looks like the airline; Carol looks like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The hymen is the membrane traditionally taken as a sign of virginity, broken at first intercourse.

clue.text: Regards exercise as early sign of excessive masturbation?

parts.note: to eye is to look at, so regards gives eyes
train as a verb, to exercise

explanation.surface: Treats a workout as the first symptom of too much self-abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the old schoolboy myth that masturbating makes you go blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness of the eyes, the first step on the road to the blindness of playground legend.
